12d-orbital.lens: conductor / performance coherence (choreography, animation timing, notation grammar, motion-fidelity)

findings.claim: The prefers-reduced-motion guard is inert: it silences nothing that actually moves, so a reduced-motion user still gets the full 4-minute ballet, the symphony sweep, and the epoch orbit.
findings.evidence: Line 62 is the ONLY reduced-motion handling: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}}`. grep confirms no `matchMedia`/`prefers-reduced` anywhere in the JS. But 100% of this artifact's motion is canvas pixels driven by `requestAnimationFrame` (`balletFrame`, the symphony `step`, the DILATION/CHRONOS `play` loop) — none of it is CSS animation or transition, so the `*{animation:none;transition:none}` rule is a no-op for every moving thing on screen.
findings.fix: Honor the preference in JS, don't just appear to. Read `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)').matches` once; when true, snap performances to their final pose instead of tweening — set `BAL.cur[id]=T[id]` (skip the per-frame `1-exp` follow), suppress the M/P/D orbits/breathing, and stop the epoch-orbit auto-advance (jump epochs on keypress only). Register-honest alternative if you won't wire it: delete the line-62 rule so the page doesn't advertise a guard it doesn't keep.

findings.claim: The narrated climax projection is not enforced: the 'collapse×superposition at the climax' claim depends on the DIAMOND movement landing on TOUR index 6, but movement type and axis choice are computed from two unrelated inputs.
findings.evidence: Movement type F (M/P/W/D/T) comes from MIDI note-density/velocity in `buildForms`; the projection axes come from `TOUR[segI % TOUR.length]` (line 710), where `TOUR[6]=[8,9]` is the D9 COLLAPSE × D10 SUPERPOSITION pair. Nothing couples the 'D' segment to segI==6. The help text (line 132) and code comment (632-633) both promise 'collapse×superposition AT THE CLIMAX', but for any piece whose velocity-peak segment isn't the 7th, the visual climax (diamonds center-stage) renders under whatever unrelated axes segI%10 yields.
findings.fix: Couple the projection to the meaning, not the segment ordinal: drive axes from F via a per-movement map (e.g. `D → [8,9]`, `M → [9,10]`, `P → [10,5]`) inside the segment-change block, so the climax always sounds/looks its narrated projection. If you keep the ordinal tour, soften the copy to 'the tour passes through collapse×superposition' rather than 'at the climax'.

findings.claim: An internal comment overstates motion-fidelity: it asserts the dancers never leave their data, but three of the four movements add invented offsets on top of the true pose.
findings.evidence: Lines 630-631 comment: 'the dancers glide because the world turns, not because they leave their data.' Yet in `balletTargets` the M movement adds `Math.sin(ts*1.6+i)*6` breathing to superposed nodes (674-675), P replaces positions with a radius-20 orbit around the projected midpoint (680-681), and D replaces diamond/meta positions with a rotating `cx+cos(a)*S*.2` circle (690-697). Only W (and the axis swaps) are genuine re-projections; M/P/D genuinely leave the data.

Reword to something like 'in the epoch-wave and projection swaps the dancers move because the world turns; the character movements are choreography, and the coda returns every node to its data position.' The user-facing copy already gets this right ('The dance ends where truth is') — align the comment so the code doesn't contradict itself.

findings.claim: The five META-family node drawers assert precise evidentiary-road counts that the embedded lattice does not contain — the page renders and sonifies these nodes at hardness 0 with zero connections, while their prose describes them as the graph's most-connected story.
findings.evidence: In the lattice JSON, meta_ont.what = "Receives 31 evidentiary roads but emits almost nothing"; meta_lib.what = "17 documents, 64 roads out — and in-degree ZERO"; meta_ety = "Pure exporter: 8 roads out, 0 in"; meta_met = "24 library roads vs 8 epistemology roads in". But `edges` contains 0 edges touching any of meta_ont/epi/met/ety/lib (verified: `edges touching ANY meta node: 0`). So `hard(meta_lib,8)=0` → in the symphony `if (hd===0) return;` (line 845) means the meta-family is literally never sounded, and in the plot they collapse to the hardness-0/in-deg-0 corner. The page's own honesty note (line 113) says "this is a computed projection of the lattice," and the D1 law is "hardness = count of DISTINCT domains among in-edge source nodes" — the 31/64/8/24 counts are fabricated relative to that computation.
findings.fix: Either add the ~31/64/8 edges the prose asserts (so hardness, sound, and position match the story), or strip the integer road-counts from the meta drawers and state plainly that the family-scale connectivity analysis is external to this lattice. Cut is cleaner: a node described as 'receives 31 roads' cannot render silent and unconnected.
findings._lens: skeptic — where the artifact overclaims or lies about its own fidelity

findings.claim: The symphony copy guarantees "no semitone clashes ... by construction" in the same breath that it unlocks maj7 and 9 — but maj7 puts a semitone into the scale, and the pitch-quantizer actually emits adjacent semitone notes at later epochs.
findings.evidence: Help drawer (line 132): "maj7 and 9 unlock at later epochs — Debussy/Satie by construction, no semitone clashes." Code: `offs=[0,2,4,7,9]; if(k>=6)offs.push(11); if(k>=7)offs.push(14)` (lines 799-801). With root Db the scale pc-set becomes {0,1,3,5,8,10} — pc 0 and pc 1 are a semitone apart. Simulating `quant(40+y*45,deg)` across the Y range yields adjacent MIDI pairs 48-49, 60-61, 72-73, 84-85 — real semitone/minor-second clashes two nodes can sound together. The 'by construction' guarantee holds only for the pure pentatonic (k=5, early epochs).
findings.fix: Drop 'no semitone clashes' or qualify it to the pentatonic core: say the base scale is clash-free and that maj7/9 add a deliberate tension at later epochs. Don't assert an invariant the same clause voids.
findings._lens: skeptic — where the artifact overclaims or lies about its own fidelity

findings.claim: "Change any control and the music must change — that is the test" fails for its own trails layer: the trails echo is wired once at symphony start and does not respond to toggling trails during playback, unlike the other three layers which re-read per measure.
findings.evidence: Help drawer (line 132) states the test explicitly. `entangle`/`invariants`/`satoshi` are read inside `symMeasure` every measure (`if(showEnt)` L859, `if(showSat)` L864, `if(showInv)` L870), so they change the next measure. But the trails echo delay graph is built only inside `toggleSymph` (`if (trails){...createDelay...}` L885-889), and the trails toggle handler is just `toggle('t-trail', v => trails = v)` (L418) — no audio rebuild. Toggling trails mid-symphony changes nothing audible.
findings.fix: Either make the trails toggle live (route through/around the delay on change) or soften the claim to 'most controls' — the artifact set itself a falsifiable test and one control fails it.

findings.claim: The ballet's projection-tour narration names a fixed meaningful climax projection ("collapse×superposition at the climax") that the code does not guarantee — the axis sequence is indexed by raw segment number, decoupled from the data-driven movement forms.
findings.evidence: Help drawer (line 132) and code comment (L629-633): "kinematics → degrees → entropy → collapse×superposition at the climax." But `TOUR` is a fixed 10-entry array (L634) indexed as `TOUR[segI % TOUR.length]` (L710), while the Diamond climax form 'D' is assigned by `buildForms` per note-density/velocity (L558-559) and can land on any segment index. So the [8,9] collapse×superposition projection (TOUR index 6) is not pinned to the 'D' climax segment — the stated correspondence is coincidental, not enforced.
findings.fix: Bind the projection to the form (e.g. pick the X·Y pair from PROGRAM[form], so the Diamond movement always renders collapse×superposition), or describe the tour as an independent axis cycle rather than one keyed to the movements.

findings.claim: The '720° pressure test' is presented as the gate that crystallizes a node, but the code performs none of it — crystallization is pure in-edge counting.
findings.evidence: Modal rule-box: "a node crystallizes only when it survives both sweeps AND holds ≥4 in-edges from distinct uncorrelated domains." But the only crystallization trigger in code is `hardness(n,ep) >= 4`, and `hardness` is just `doms.size` over `EDGES.forEach(e => ... doms.add(byId[e[0]].dom))`. No LAB/BAR/Bayesian/COURT/Recoil/KKL/FunHouse sweep is ever evaluated. The drawer then hard-codes the verdict for anything with 4 edges: `hd>=4 ? 'survived — orthogonal echo confirmed' : ...` and `anterior sweep = filed in meta-audit gauntlet · posterior sweep = survived`. Every diamond gets 'survived', regardless of the node's actual status.
findings.fix: Drop the 'survives both sweeps AND' precondition from the rule-box (the code only counts edges), or make the drawer say what it measures: 'hardness N — N distinct source domains.' Don't assert a sweep the artifact doesn't run.

findings.claim: The drawer asserts 'orthogonal echo confirmed' for diamonds, directly contradicting the artifact's own nodes that say the echo detector isn't running, and dressing a tag-count as measured orthogonality.
findings.evidence: Drawer string: "survived — orthogonal echo confirmed". HUD copy: "Hardness is EARNED: distinct uncorrelated domains pointing at the same node." Yet the same JSON says the Orthogonal Echo Detector is "RC-OPS-001 gated behind an Observatory period — not ROM", the goal lattice is "gated at 100 receipts", and the Folksonomist "Runs on synthetic corpora only until 100R". The metric under all of it is `doms.add(byId[e[0]].dom)` — the count of distinct author-assigned `dom` tags on hand-drawn edges. 'Uncorrelated / orthogonal / confirmed' claims independence and a detection event that the code neither measures nor, by its own admission, can run yet.
findings.fix: Say 'distinct authored domains' not 'uncorrelated/orthogonal', and cut 'echo confirmed' — the node's own text admits the echo detector is gated. Hardness = tag-distinctness of hand-authored edges; label it as such.

findings.claim: The Resolution ladder overclaims: its top two stops ('8K' and 'LOSSLESS') render identical pixels, and '8K' at factor 1 is native devicePixelRatio, nowhere near 8K.
findings.evidence: `RES_STOPS = [['8-BIT',.055],['32MB',.14],['2K',.38],['4K',.68],['8K',1],['LOSSLESS',1]]` — 8K and LOSSLESS are both factor 1, so `cv.width = clientWidth*devicePixelRatio*1` is identical for both. Sliding 8K→LOSSLESS changes zero pixels; the only difference is `LOSSLESS` disabling label culling (`if (LOSSLESS || z >= minZ ...)`). The comment claims "real pixels, not a filter... no information dropped", but the named resolution climb flatlines at the top and the highest 'quality' rung is a label-culling toggle, not more resolution.
findings.fix: Either give LOSSLESS a genuinely higher factor, or rename the top rung so it doesn't promise resolution it doesn't add (e.g. '8K' → 'NATIVE', 'LOSSLESS' → 'ALL LABELS').

findings.claim: Gold is overloaded: any node reaching 4 domains is force-filled gold, discarding its status color, so the legend's color code is unreadable for exactly the most important nodes.
findings.evidence: Legend: "■ formalized [green] · ■ needs truing [gold] · ■ needs shoring [red] · ■ gated [steel]". But diamonds render `ctx.fillStyle = hd>=4 ? '#FFD700' : c` — gold regardless of status. So a formalized 'ok' node like `rec`/`sup`/`noto` (all status 'ok', all diamonds) shows gold, which the legend reads as 'needs truing'. The one color channel that encodes truth-state is overwritten by the hardness channel at the top of the lattice.
findings.fix: Encode diamond-ness in the halo/shape (already present) and keep the fill on the status color, so a formalized diamond doesn't read as 'needs truing'.

findings.claim: Legend implies distinct glyphs for crystal vs diamond, but the canvas draws the same 4-point diamond shape for both.

In `draw`, the `else` branch (hd>=3) draws one shape — `moveTo(n.x,n.y-dr) ... lineTo` a 4-point rhombus — for both hd===3 and hd>=4; they differ only by color, halo and size, not glyph. The two distinct legend glyphs (◆ vs ◈) set an expectation the render doesn't meet.
findings.fix: Match the legend to what's drawn (same glyph, 'crystal 3 / diamond 4+ = brighter+haloed'), or actually vary the polygon for hd>=4.
